problem.title: Cloud Object Storage (S3 / GCS) KMS Key Throttling Under Mass Downloads
problem.prompt: Data analytics cluster downloading 30,000 encrypted S3 objects per second using AWS KMS customer managed keys.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Enable S3 Bucket Keys on KMS-encrypted buckets to eliminate KMS control-plane request throttling under heavy I/O."
Production Hardening: Enable S3 Bucket Keys for SSE-KMS, which reduces KMS API calls by up to 99% by generating an ephemeral bucket-level data key that caches locally within S3 for temporary reuse.
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.
constraints: Incident Scenario Baseline: Data analytics cluster downloading 30,000 encrypted S3 objects per second using AWS KMS customer managed keys.
Failure Cascade Path: 100k QPS → TTL Expiration → Cache Miss Herd → Origin Slam → 💥 DB Meltdown
Sub-millisecond rejection / shed latency for overloaded requests

stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: 100k QPS → TTL Expiration → Cache Miss Herd → Origin Slam → 💥 DB Meltdown.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Every S3 Decrypt operation calls the AWS KMS API. The account hits the AWS KMS requests-per-second quota (e.g. 10,000 req/s), throwing KMS ThrottlingException and failing all analytics jobs.
Breakdown Chain: 100k QPS → TTL Expiration → Cache Miss Herd → Origin Slam → 💥 DB Meltdown
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.

tradeOffs: Architectural Invariant: "Enable S3 Bucket Keys on KMS-encrypted buckets to eliminate KMS control-plane request throttling under heavy I/O."
Physical Resource Boundary: Dynamic admission control ensures worker threads never buffer dead requests during downstream brownouts.
approachSteps: 1. Track real-time latency gradients and inflight concurrency.
2. Reject excess traffic at the ingress boundary within <0.1ms.
3. Monitor P99 latency and verify autonomous recovery when downstream pressure subsides.
